title: Snow in India: Where and When to See It (A Guide from Himachal)
seo_title: Snow in India: Where & When to See It, Month by Month
seo_desc: Where to see snow in India: Shimla, Manali and Solang, Dharamshala, Auli and Gulmarg — official snowfall figures, ski seasons, roads and how to plan.
label: Snow in India
blurb: Where and when to see snow — Shimla, Manali, Solang, Auli, Gulmarg — with official figures
sub: Yes, you can see snow in India — in the Himalayan hill towns of the north, mostly from December to February. Here is where it falls, what the official figures say in °C and °F, where you can ski, which roads close, and how to fit snow into a trip to India. Written by a travel company based in Himachal.
hero_alt: Snow on the roofs of Shimla's hillside houses, snow peaks above the deodar forest at Solang near Manali, the Dhauladhar range at sunset above Dharamshala, and the winter snowfield of Gulmarg
q: Where can you see snow in India?
answer: In the Himalayan north, mostly from December to February. The easiest places to reach are the Himachal hill towns — Shimla, Manali with Solang valley, and Dharamshala — by car from Delhi. Auli in Uttarakhand and Gulmarg in Kashmir are ski areas; check government travel advice for Kashmir. Snow is likely but never guaranteed. Send us your dates for a quote.

sections.h2: When does it snow in India? The official figures
sections.lead: January and February are the snowiest months in the Himachal hills. December can bring snow but usually less of it. The India Meteorological Department's long-term figures for Shimla:
items: 16 in — in January, and again in February
of snow a month in January and February
sections.note: Shimla's district administration says nights in December–January fall to about 0 °C (32 °F) and that warm clothing and a jacket are a must. March can still bring a little snow (about 7 cm on average). Manali, higher up, is colder. More detail in our best time to visit Himachal guide.

sections.h2: Skiing and snow play: Solang, Auli and Gulmarg
sections.lead: India has a few real ski areas. They suit beginners and a holiday day on the snow more than a European-style ski week:
items: Himachal Pradesh Tourism says that in winter the snow-packed slopes become a ski arena where state and national championships are held. There is a gondola (ropeway). It is a day trip from Manali, 13 km (8 mi) away.

Run by the state's GMVN: a chair lift and a ski lift, with the ski season starting in December and snow until March. Auli lies at 2,500–3,050 m (8,200–10,000 ft) — a long mountain drive from Dehradun airport.
India's best-known ski area: a gondola up to about 3,980 m and a government-run ski shop. Read the government advice first — see our Gulmarg guide.
Just want to touch the snow?
Shimla, Manali and McLeod Ganj in January and February are the easy answer: snow-covered towns and forests, cosy hotels and mountain views, without needing to ski.

sections.h2: Winter roads: why we drive in daylight only
sections.text: The UK Foreign Office advises: "Avoid travelling at night and in fog as accidents are common due to low visibility." Snow can close mountain roads for a day or more, and Rohtang Pass stays shut from late November until about May. So we drive the hills only in daylight, keep a spare day in every snow trip, and re-route when a road closes.

faqs: Where can I see snow in India?

In the Himalayan north. The easiest places for a visitor are the Himachal hill towns — Shimla, Manali with Solang valley, and Dharamshala/McLeod Ganj — all reachable by car from Delhi. Auli in Uttarakhand and Gulmarg in Kashmir are ski areas.
Which month does it snow in India?

Mostly December to February. In Shimla the India Meteorological Department's averages are about 7 cm in December and about 40 cm in each of January and February, with roughly four snow days a month. Snow is never guaranteed on a given date.
Does it snow in Shimla and Manali in December?

It can. December snowfall in Shimla averages about 7 cm, so a white Christmas is possible but not certain. January and February are the better bet. Manali is colder, and in winter the Solang slopes near Manali become a ski area.

Yes — at Solang near Manali, at Auli in Uttarakhand (chair lift and ski lift, season from December) and at Gulmarg in Kashmir. They suit beginners and snow days more than a long ski holiday. For Gulmarg, read the UK and US government advice first.
Is it safe to go to Gulmarg for snow?

The UK FCDO advises against all travel to Jammu and Kashmir except Jammu city, and the US State Department says 'Do not travel' to J&K except eastern Ladakh and Leh (checked 23 Oct 2026). Travel insurance may not cover you against FCDO advice. Himachal is our suggested alternative.
Is Rohtang Pass open in winter?

No. Heavy snow closes Rohtang Pass from late November until about May, according to Himachal Pradesh Tourism. In winter the Atal Tunnel keeps the road from Manali to Lahaul open, and Solang is the usual snow day.
How cold is it, and what should I pack?

Shimla averages 2.5–10.3 °C (37–51 °F) in January and nights fall to about 0 °C (32 °F); Manali can drop below −5 °C (23 °F). Bring warm layers, a jacket, gloves, a hat and shoes with grip. If you have health concerns, consult your doctor.
